issues.description: font-weight-notation: HAS_NAMED regex is case-insensitive and may match identifiers inside url(...) or font-family parts of the font shorthand, causing false skips
issues.detail: The precondition for the fast-path skip is: 'decl.value contains no token that could trigger a rename'. But \b...\b with case-insensitive flag on font-weight keywords like 'normal', 'bold', 'light', 'bolder' will also match inside font-family identifiers within the font shorthand (e.g. font: 12px/1 "Bold Sans";). Conversely, named-where-possible skips when no \b\d{3}\b appears, but \d{3} may also match parts of unrelated numeric tokens in the font shorthand (line-height, size). The author has not stated the invariant being preserved across this fast path. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation: HAS_PERCENTAGE anchors on ^|[,\s] while HAS_KEYWORD uses \b; asymmetric anchoring is unjustified
issues.detail: The invariant the author needs is: 'if selectorRegex does not match rule.selector, the rule body would have produced no diagnostic'. HAS_PERCENTAGE uses (?:^|[,\s]) to avoid matching '50%' as substring of something else; HAS_KEYWORD uses \b. These two anchoring strategies are not derived from a single specification — they are intuited per-rule. State why each anchoring is sufficient, or unify them.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation: walkRules(/:/, ...) replaces a named guard with an opaque regex argument
issues.detail: The pre-existing check was ruleNode.selector.includes(':') with the comment 'get out early if no pseudo elements or classes'. The replacement walkRules(/:/, fn) is semantically equivalent to the skip condition (both treat selector as a string), but the meaning is now invisible: a reader must know that postcss walkRules(regex, fn) tests regex against node.selector. Structured programming says: name your invariants. This is a SMUGGLED-GOTO via library affordance — control flow is now controlled by the library's regex handling, not by visible code.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation: 'prefix' guard /[<>]/ assumes < and > only appear as range operators
issues.detail: Precondition for skipping in primary='prefix' mode: 'no <,> anywhere in atRule.params'. The character class /[<>]/ will also fire on these characters inside strings or attribute-like constructs within @media params (rare but not impossible in malformed/extended syntax). More importantly, the 'context' guard /(?:min|max)-/i is case-insensitive — CSS feature names are case-insensitive so this is intentional, but the author did not state that as the justifying invariant. State preconditions explicitly.

issues.description: No tests added to demonstrate the fast-path invariant: 'skipped declarations would not have produced a warning'
issues.detail: The author claims this is a performance fix. The correctness obligation is that for every input the original rule would have flagged, the new rule still flags it — extensional equivalence. The diff adds no tests. The changeset entry says 'Fixed: *-notation performance' — performance is being fixed, but correctness is being asserted by silence. The existing suite presumably passes, but boundary cases that LOOK skippable but are not have not been added. TESTED-NOT-PROVED.

The else branch assigns /./ to mean 'match anything', i.e. no filter. A reader must reason: '/./ matches any non-empty string, so walkRules(/./, fn) is equivalent to walkRules(fn) for any non-empty selector'. Empty selectors do not exist in valid postcss rules, so this is safe. Worth a comment naming the invariant explicitly rather than encoding it as a sentinel regex.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED in font-weight-notation deduplicates two source arrays silently via Set
issues.detail: [...new Set([...fontWeightNonNumericKeywords, ...fontWeightRelativeKeywords])] is correct but obscures whether the two source arrays were expected to overlap. If they did not overlap, the Set is dead code; if they did, the reader cannot tell from this expression which keywords are shared. State the invariant or add a comment.

issues.description: import-notation guards are correct but the underlying invariant is unstated
issues.detail: The two guards are mutually correct: if primary='string' and params contains no 'url(', the value is already a string — nothing to flag. If primary='url' and params contains 'url(', the value is already url — nothing to flag. This is sound. But the author did not write the one-line comment that would make this obvious to a future maintainer. REASONED, but only barely, and only by the reader, not by the author.

review.summary: This patch is a textbook case of TESTED-NOT-PROVED. The author is optimizing six rules by adding fast-path skip guards, but nowhere in the diff or description is the correctness invariant stated: 'for every declaration/at-rule/selector the original rule would have warned on, the new guard does not skip it.' That invariant is the entire point of the change, and it must be reasoned about, not merely benchmarked. Several guards — the case-insensitive \\b on font-weight keywords in the font shorthand, the asymmetric anchoring between HAS_PERCENTAGE and HAS_KEYWORD, the bare /:/ replacing a named comment — are plausibly correct but not visibly correct. A reader cannot follow the reasoning without simulating the program. No new tests lock the boundary. I would refuse this in its current form and require: explicit per-guard comments stating the skip-precondition, targeted tests for cases that look skippable but must not be, and a consistent anchoring strategy across the regexes.
